project.name: vertex-ai-firebase-angular-example
project.description: Vertex AI in Firebase x Angular starter kit: an Angular 19 client app that uses the Firebase AI Logic SDK (Gemini via AngularFire) for AI-powered product features, with a signal-based product catalog and an AI chat/function-calling service.

nodes.name: ai.service.ts
nodes.summary: Core AI service wrapping Firebase AI Logic (Vertex AI) that initializes a Gemini 2.0 Flash generative model with function-calling tools and manages a multi-turn chat session to answer product questions and manipulate the cart.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses @angular/fire/vertexai for Vertex AI integration; declares FunctionDeclarationsTool with Schema builders at construction time; dispatches tool calls (getNumberOfProducts, getProducts, addToCart) inside an async ask() loop using function-calling protocol.

nodes.name: AiService
nodes.summary: Injectable singleton that wraps Vertex AI chat session lifecycle: constructs a GenerativeModel with system instructions and a tool set, then exposes ask(), getProducts(), getNumberOfProducts(), and addToCart() to route between the AI model and ProductService.
nodes.languageNotes: Registers three function declarations as tools on the Gemini model so the model can invoke them via function-calling; the ask() method handles the function-response round-trip before returning the final text response.

nodes.name: app.component.ts
nodes.summary: Root standalone Angular component that renders the NG-STORE shopping UI with a product grid and an AI-powered chat panel; manages message history and product list via Angular signals and delegates AI queries to AiService.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Angular 19 standalone component with inline template; leverages signal(), viewChild(), and effect() for reactive state and DOM side effects (auto-scroll chat history).

nodes.name: AppComponent
nodes.summary: Standalone root component binding the product listing and AI chat window; injects AiService and ProductService, maintains messageHistory and productList signals, and exposes addToCart() and submitMessage() event handlers.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses effect() to auto-scroll the chat history container whenever messageHistory signal updates; submitMessage() is async and awaits AiService.ask().

nodes.name: message.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the Message interface representing a single chat message with a sender discriminant ('user' | 'agent') and text content, used across the AppComponent chat panel.

nodes.name: product.service.ts
nodes.summary: Injectable service that manages the product catalog (10 hardcoded grocery items) and shopping cart state using Angular signals; exposes getProducts(), getCart(), and addToCart() for use by both AppComponent and AiService.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Angular signal() for reactive cart state and computed() to derive the running cart total; productCartTotal is a computed signal so consumers get automatic updates.

nodes.name: ProductService
nodes.summary: Root-provided injectable managing an in-memory product list and a reactive cart; productCart is a writable signal updated by addToCart(), and productCartTotal is a computed signal for the running price total.
nodes.languageNotes: providedIn: 'root' ensures a single shared instance across AiService and AppComponent; signals eliminate the need for explicit change detection.

nodes.name: product.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the Product interface with name, price, and image fields, serving as the shared data contract between ProductService, AiService, and AppComponent.

nodes.name: app.config.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the root Angular application configuration object (appConfig), bootstrapping AngularFire, provideFirebaseApp, provideAuth, and the router using the project's Firebase environment settings and route definitions.

nodes.name: app.routes.ts
nodes.summary: Declares the top-level Angular route array (routes) that maps URL paths to lazily or eagerly loaded components for this application.

nodes.name: environment.ts
nodes.summary: Exports the production environment configuration object containing Firebase project credentials and feature flags used at runtime.

nodes.name: main.ts
nodes.summary: Application entry point that bootstraps the Angular standalone AppComponent using the root appConfig, kicking off the entire application lifecycle.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Project overview and getting-started guide for the Vertex AI in Firebase x Angular Starter Kit, covering Firebase project setup, environment configuration, and running the app with `ng serve`.

nodes.name: angular.json
nodes.summary: Angular CLI workspace configuration defining the single-app project build pipeline, dev-server targets, schematics defaults (inline templates/styles, tests skipped), bundle budgets, and environment file replacements for production vs. development builds.
nodes.languageNotes: All schematics defaults disable test generation (skipTests: true), indicating this starter kit intentionally ships without test scaffolding.

nodes.name: firebase.json
nodes.summary: Firebase project configuration file — currently empty, indicating Firebase hosting or emulator rules have not yet been configured.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: npm package manifest declaring Angular 19 and AngularFire dependencies, along with build scripts (`ng serve`, `ng build`) for the vertex-ai-firebase-angular-example application.

nodes.name: tsconfig.app.json
nodes.summary: Application-specific TypeScript configuration that extends the root `tsconfig.json`, scoping compilation to `src/main.ts` and ambient declaration files under `src/`.

nodes.name: tsconfig.json
nodes.summary: Root TypeScript compiler configuration enabling strict mode, ES2022 targets, bundler module resolution, experimental decorators, and Angular-specific strict template checking options.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `moduleResolution: bundler` (TypeScript 5.0+) and enables `experimentalDecorators` required for Angular's decorator-based component model.

nodes.name: app.component.css
nodes.summary: Component-scoped stylesheet for AppComponent defining the page header layout, responsive product card grid, and chat agent window UI including message bubbles for the AI assistant interaction panel.
nodes.languageNotes: Relies on CSS custom properties (--primary, --secondary) declared in the global styles.css. Uses CSS Grid for the product listing and the main two-column container layout.

nodes.name: environment.development.ts
nodes.summary: Development environment configuration file exporting an environment object with production set to false and a placeholder empty firebase config object. Used by the Angular build system for development-mode builds.

nodes.name: index.html
nodes.summary: Angular application host HTML page that provides the minimal HTML shell, sets the base href for client-side routing, and mounts the root Angular component via the <app-root> custom element.

nodes.name: styles.css
nodes.summary: Global CSS reset and design token definitions applying a normalized box model baseline to common HTML elements and declaring CSS custom properties (--primary, --secondary) for the application's color theme.

layers.name: UI Layer
layers.description: The root Angular component, its scoped stylesheet, the host HTML shell, and the global CSS reset and design tokens that together render the NG-STORE product grid and AI chat panel in the browser.

layers.name: AI & Business Services
layers.description: The Vertex AI in Firebase (Gemini) chat service and the Angular signals-based product catalog and cart service that together implement the AI-powered shopping assistant logic.

layers.name: Domain Models
layers.description: Shared TypeScript interfaces — Product and Message — that define the data contracts consumed by the UI, AI service, and product service throughout the application.

layers.name: App Bootstrap & Firebase Configuration
layers.description: The application entry point, root Angular provider configuration (AngularFire, Auth, Router), route definitions, and environment files that initialize Firebase connectivity and launch the app.

layers.name: Build Configuration
layers.description: Angular CLI workspace settings, Firebase project config, npm package manifest, and TypeScript compiler options that govern how the application is built, bundled, and type-checked.

layers.name: Project Support
layers.description: Developer-facing documentation (getting-started guide and Firebase setup instructions) and tooling meta-configuration (Understand-Anything ignore patterns) that support project onboarding and analysis tooling.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: The README introduces the Vertex AI in Firebase x Angular Starter Kit and explains the one prerequisite before anything runs: creating a Firebase project and populating `src/environments/environment.ts` with your project credentials. Reading it first sets the context for every configuration file and service you will encounter in the tour.

tour.title: Application Entry Point
tour.description: The Angular bootstrap lives in `src/main.ts`, which calls `bootstrapApplication(AppComponent, appConfig)` to start the entire app. This single line wires the root component to the provider configuration and kicks off Angular's change-detection and dependency-injection systems.
tour.languageLesson: Angular 19 standalone bootstrap replaces NgModule-based `platformBrowserDynamic().bootstrapModule()`. The second argument to `bootstrapApplication` is an `ApplicationConfig` object, not a module, making the DI tree explicit and tree-shakable.

tour.title: Firebase Configuration & Environment
tour.description: `environment.ts` holds the Firebase project credentials (apiKey, projectId, appId, etc.) that every Firebase SDK call depends on. This is the file the README tells you to fill in — without valid values here, the app connects to nothing.

tour.title: Provider Setup — AngularFire & Router
tour.description: `app.config.ts` consumes the environment object from Step 3 and registers `provideFirebaseApp`, `provideAuth`, and the Angular Router as root-level providers. This is where Firebase is initialized for the Angular DI system, making the `AngularFirestore` and `VertexAI` tokens injectable anywhere in the app.
tour.languageLesson: Angular's `ApplicationConfig.providers` array replaces `@NgModule.imports`. Each `provide*` factory (from `@angular/fire`, `@angular/router`) returns a `Provider[]` that Angular merges into the root injector, keeping third-party initialization colocated and auditable.

tour.title: Root UI Component
tour.description: `app.component.ts` is the single page the user sees: a product grid on the left and an AI chat panel on the right. It injects `AiService` and `ProductService`, holds `messageHistory` and `productList` as Angular signals, and exposes `submitMessage()` (which awaits the AI) and `addToCart()` event handlers.
tour.languageLesson: Angular 19 signals (`signal()`, `computed()`, `effect()`) replace Zone.js-driven change detection for reactive state. The `effect()` call in AppComponent watches `messageHistory` and auto-scrolls the chat container, demonstrating a side-effect pattern that replaces `ngAfterViewChecked`.

tour.title: UI Styles
tour.description: `styles.css` declares the global CSS custom properties (`--primary`, `--secondary`) and a box-model reset that all component styles inherit from. `app.component.css` uses those tokens along with CSS Grid to lay out the two-column product-plus-chat page and style the AI message bubbles.

tour.title: AI Service — Firebase AI Logic Core
tour.description: `ai.service.ts` is the heart of the application: it initializes a Gemini 2.0 Flash generative model via `@angular/fire/vertexai`, registers three function-calling tools (`getProducts`, `getNumberOfProducts`, `addToCart`), and exposes a single `ask()` method that manages the multi-turn chat session and routes function-call responses back to `ProductService`.
tour.languageLesson: Gemini function calling works in a round-trip loop: the model returns a `FunctionCall` part instead of text, the client executes the real function and sends back a `FunctionResponse`, and the model then produces the final text reply. `AiService.ask()` implements this loop explicitly before resolving its promise.

tour.title: Product Service — Catalog & Cart State
tour.description: `product.service.ts` maintains the in-memory product catalog (10 hardcoded grocery items) and the shopping cart as Angular signals. Both `AppComponent` (for display) and `AiService` (via function-call tools) call into this service, making it the single source of truth for product and cart state.
tour.languageLesson: `computed()` signals derive new values from other signals without manual subscription management. `productCartTotal` in `ProductService` is a computed signal over `productCart`, so any read of it in a template or effect is automatically tracked and re-evaluated when the cart changes.

tour.title: Domain Models
tour.description: `product.ts` defines the `Product` interface (name, price, image) and `message.ts` defines the `Message` interface (sender: `'user' | 'agent'`, text). These two files are the shared data contracts that `ProductService`, `AiService`, and `AppComponent` all depend on — understanding them is key to reading any other file in the app.
tour.languageLesson: TypeScript discriminated unions (the `sender: 'user' | 'agent'` literal union on `Message`) let the template and rendering logic branch by type with full type-narrowing, eliminating the need for boolean flags like `isAgentMessage`.

tour.title: Build & TypeScript Configuration
tour.description: `package.json` declares the Angular 19 and AngularFire dependency versions and the `ng serve` / `ng build` scripts. `angular.json` configures the build pipeline — including the environment file swap between `environment.ts` and `environment.development.ts` — while `tsconfig.json` and `tsconfig.app.json` enable strict mode, ES2022 targets, and bundler module resolution required by Angular's decorator model.
tour.languageLesson: Angular CLI's `fileReplacements` in `angular.json` swaps `environment.development.ts` for `environment.ts` at build time for production. `tsconfig.json` sets `moduleResolution: bundler` (TypeScript 5.0+), which correctly resolves package exports fields without requiring `node16` or `nodenext`.
